methods.name: Basic Research
methods.description: Research done to understand how something works, without a specific practical problem to solve. It builds general knowledge that other research can use later.

methods.name: Applied Research
methods.description: Research aimed at solving a specific, real-world problem. The goal is a practical answer someone can act on.

methods.name: Exploratory Research
methods.description: Early research on a topic that isn't well understood yet. It helps figure out what questions to ask and what to look at more closely.

methods.name: Field Research
methods.description: Collecting data by watching or talking to people in their real setting, like a workplace, classroom or neighborhood, instead of a lab.

methods.name: Market Research
methods.description: Research about customers and markets: what people want, what they would buy, and how they see a product or its competitors.

methods.name: Qualitative Research
methods.description: Explores people's reasons, feelings and experiences through interviews, focus groups and open-ended questions. Good for learning the why.

methods.name: Quantitative Research
methods.description: Uses numbers and measurements, like rating-scale surveys or counts, and looks at them with statistics. Good for how many or how much.

methods.name: Mixed Methods
methods.description: Combines qualitative and quantitative research in one study, so you get both the numbers and the reasons behind them.

methods.name: Randomized Controlled Trial
methods.description: Randomly splits people into groups, changes something for one group, and compares the results. The strongest way to test if something actually causes an effect.

methods.name: Policy Research
methods.description: Studies how laws, rules or programs work and what effects they have, to help decision makers choose or improve a policy.

methods.name: Systematic Review
methods.description: Gathers and evaluates all the existing studies on a question with a clear, repeatable process, to sum up what the evidence says overall.

methods.name: Product R&D
methods.description: Research and development to design, build and test a new product, or improve an existing one, before it launches.

methods.name: Longitudinal Research
methods.description: Studies the same people or things again and again over a long time to see how they change.
